findings.title: Configured batch sizes can exceed non-SQLite parameter limits
findings.body: The new delete path binds one SQL parameter per selected ID, but only SQLite is handled specially. Grafana also supports SQL Server, which rejects statements with more than 2100 parameters; a configured annotation cleanup batch size such as the 32767 value exercised by this PR will therefore make cleanup fail on SQL Server. MySQL/PostgreSQL also have finite prepared-statement parameter limits. The old subquery-based delete did not create one bound parameter per row. Cap/split the ID list according to the active dialect's parameter limit (or use a dialect-safe alternative) before issuing the DELETE.

findings.title: Normal cleanup batches are logged as errors with the complete ID list
findings.body: Each successful ID fetch and delete is logged through `r.log.Error`, including every selected annotation/tag ID. This emits false error events even when `err` is nil and can serialize tens of thousands of IDs for one batch (the added test configures 32767). With cleanup enabled this creates substantial log volume, error-alert noise, and potentially expensive formatting/storage on every cleanup cycle. Use an appropriate debug-level summary and avoid logging the full ID list; the same issue is repeated in the count and orphan-tag paths.

findings.title: The PR increases the frequency of every cleanup job from ten minutes to one minute
findings.body: This changes the scheduler for the entire cleanup job list, not just annotation cleanup, causing temporary-file scans and all database cleanup operations to run ten times as often. The PR description only calls for splitting annotation cleanup statements, so this unrelated change can significantly increase database/disk load and make the nine-minute cleanup window much more likely to be continuously occupied. Revert this interval change or explicitly justify and isolate a different annotation-cleanup schedule.
